title: Farming at Kuk Swamp
description: Mounds and ditches for growing taro and bananas show that the New Guinea highlanders developed agriculture independently.

title: Lapita pottery appears
description: A seafaring people making decorated pottery appear in the Bismarck Archipelago, from where their descendants settle the Pacific.

title: Torres sails the south coast
description: The Spanish navigator Luis Váez de Torres lands in the east and follows the south coast, proving that New Guinea is an island.

title: Dampier names New Britain
description: The English navigator William Dampier finds the strait that separates New Britain from New Guinea.

title: Port Moresby named
description: Captain John Moresby of the Royal Navy charts the harbour that becomes the capital.

title: German protectorate proclaimed
description: Germany raises its flag over the north-east of the island and the Bismarck Archipelago.

title: British protectorate proclaimed
description: Britain proclaims a protectorate over the south-east coast, completing the division of the island between three colonial powers.

title: Papua passes to Australia
description: British New Guinea is renamed Papua and placed under the Australian government.

title: Battle of Bita Paka
description: Australian troops take the German wireless station, and German New Guinea surrenders within days.

title: League of Nations mandate
description: Australian civil administration begins in the former German colony under a mandate from the League of Nations.

title: Highlands entered by outsiders
description: The gold prospectors Mick and Dan Leahy and the patrol officer Jim Taylor reach the Wahgi Valley, home to hundreds of thousands of people unknown to the outside world.

title: Japanese capture Rabaul
description: Japanese forces overwhelm the Australian garrison and make Rabaul their main base in the South Pacific.

title: Japanese surrender at Rabaul
description: General Imamura surrenders the Japanese forces in New Guinea and the islands on board HMS Glory.

title: Papua and New Guinea joined
polity: Territory of Papua and New Guinea
description: Australia unites the two territories under a single administration.

title: Eruption of Mount Lamington
polity: Territory of Papua and New Guinea
description: A volcano not known to be active explodes and kills about 3,000 people.

title: First general election
polity: Territory of Papua and New Guinea
description: Voters choose a House of Assembly with an indigenous majority in the first election held on universal suffrage.

title: Self-government
polity: Territory of Papua and New Guinea
description: Australia hands over internal government to a ministry led by Michael Somare.

title: Bougainville declares independence
polity: Territory of Papua and New Guinea
description: Leaders on the copper-rich island proclaim a Republic of the North Solomons two weeks before national independence, and rejoin the next year.

title: Independence from Australia
description: Papua New Guinea becomes an independent country with Michael Somare as prime minister.

title: Bougainville conflict begins
description: Landowners sabotage the Panguna copper mine, starting a war of secession that kills up to 20,000 people in ten years.

title: Rabaul destroyed by eruption
description: The volcanoes Tavurvur and Vulcan erupt together and bury most of the town in ash.

title: Sandline affair
description: The army refuses to work with mercenaries hired to end the Bougainville war, and the prime minister steps aside.

title: Aitape tsunami
description: A tsunami following an offshore earthquake kills more than 2,000 people on the north coast.

title: Bougainville Peace Agreement
description: The government and Bougainville leaders agree on autonomy for the island and a later referendum on independence.

title: Highlands earthquake
description: An earthquake of magnitude 7.5 kills about 160 people in the southern highlands.

title: Bougainville independence referendum
description: In a non-binding vote 98 per cent of Bougainvilleans choose independence from Papua New Guinea.
